newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK & China Gas sees growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: HK & China Gas sees growth in 1997.

text.p: Hong Kong and China Gas Co Ltd expects satisfactory growth in 1997, with a seven percent increase in towngas sales volume and a gain of about 65,000 new customers, chairman Lee Shau Kee said on Friday.
"The board of directors anticipates that the growth of the business will be satisfactory for 1997," Lee said in a statement attached to the company's 1996 results.
The towngas producer and supplier's basic tariff has risen by 5.2 percent since January 1, Lee said.
China Gas posted net profit of HK$1.95 billion for calendar 1996, up 19 percent from HK$1.64 billion in 1995.
Its shares were up HK$0.25 to HK$14.80 on Friday morning.
The company secured 61,543 new customers last year, bringing its installed meters to 1.17 million, Lee said.
China Gas continued to seek opportunities for investment in the gas business in China, Lee said, adding that its Zhongshan joint venture started operations in April 1996.
The company has a 45 percent interest in the King's Park Rise residential development in Kowloon, which was expected to be completed around the end of 1988, he said.
The company's network system was revalued at a fair market value of HK$19.4 billion but the revaluation surplus had not been credited to the accounts, the chairman added.
He also said Malcolm Matthews would retire as managing director with effect from May 1 and be succeeded by Alfred Chan, general manager of marketing and customer services.
